info.title: Fast Rust tools for .NET projects
info.description: Fast Rust tools for .NET formatting, linting, and affected-project detection.

commands.name: affected
commands.description: Determine projects affected by a set of Git changes

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --ignore-changed
options.description:
Ignore changes to these paths when deciding what is affected (issue #234). Repeatable; each value is a repo-relative path or a glob (`NuGet.Config`, `config/*.json`, `**/*.md`).
For CI harnesses that must REWRITE a tracked file before the tool runs — swapping in an agent-specific `NuGet.Config`, for example. `affected` compares the working tree, so such a rewrite is a genuine change and fans out exactly as a real edit to that file would; a shared feed config reaches every project. This drops those paths from the changed set.
NOTE: the global `--exclude` does NOT do this — it filters the resulting project set, not the changed files.
Every ignored file is reported on stderr: silently discarding a change is how a build under-builds and ships something untested, so it is never quiet.

options.name: --repository-path
options.description: Path to the Git repository root. Defaults to the current repository

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: --solution-path
options.description: Solution file used to limit project discovery

options.name: --from
options.description: Branch or commit to compare against --to, or against the working tree when --to is omitted

options.name: --to
options.description: Branch or commit to compare against --from

options.name: --merge-base
options.description: Compare from the merge base of --from and --to instead of directly from --from

options.name: --ci
options.description: Detect the comparison range from the CI environment (GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines, GitLab CI, or Jenkins): pull-request builds diff against the merge base with the target branch; branch (push) builds diff against the previous commit

options.name: --pr-base
options.description: Force pull-request mode: diff against the merge base of this target branch and HEAD (e.g. `--pr-base main`). Overrides --ci detection

options.name: --push
options.description: Force push/branch-build mode: diff against the current commit's parent

options.name: --base
options.description: Diff against the merge base of this ref and HEAD (generic form of --pr-base; e.g. `--base origin/develop`). Overrides --ci detection

options.name: --default-branch
options.description: Override the detected default branch (main/master) used as a fallback base for CI resolution

options.name: --fetch-base
options.description:
Minimal-fetch mode: on a shallow CI clone, fetch only the base ref (and deepen it incrementally) instead of unshallowing the whole repo. Lets CI jobs drop `fetch-depth: 0`
[alias: --minimal-fetch]

options.name: --ci-base
options.description:
Push-build baseline used by --ci. `previous-commit` preserves the provider's normal before/parent behavior; `last-successful-build` queries Azure Pipelines' Build API for the last succeeded build on this branch; `last-completed-build` also accepts a `partiallySucceeded` build, for pipelines with a `continueOnError: true` step that would otherwise never advance the baseline (issue #234)
Possible values:
- previous-commit
- last-successful-build
- last-completed-build:  `last-successful-build`, but a `partiallySucceeded` build also counts (issue #234): a pipeline with a `continueOnError: true` step never reaches `succeeded`, so the baseline never advances and the comparison window grows without bound
[default: previous-commit]

options.name: --on-missing-base
options.description:
Fallback when --from/--to/--base remains unresolvable after shallow-clone recovery: fail (default), treat every project as affected, or emit none
[default: error]
[possible values: error, all, empty]

options.name: --ci-base-fallback
options.description:
Fallback when `--ci-base last-successful-build` itself can't complete (missing SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN/Azure vars, no prior successful build, first build on a new branch). `previous-commit` (default) narrows to HEAD~1 — which silently under-builds a batched trigger; `all` conservatively builds every project; `error` fails loudly. Distinct from --on-missing-base, which governs an unresolvable explicit --from/--to/--base
[possible values: previous-commit, all, error]

options.name: --assume-changes
options.description: Assume the provided project names or paths changed instead of reading Git diff

options.name: --all
options.description:
Treat every discovered project as affected (force-full-build mode): skip the Git diff entirely and emit all projects in the chosen formats. Accepts an optional boolean so a CI toggle is an argument, not control flow: bare `--all` (or `--all=true`/`1`/`yes`/`on`) forces full; `--all=false`/`0`/`no` is off; absent (or `DOTNET_FAST_ALL` unset) is off
[env: DOTNET_FAST_ALL=]
[default: false]
[possible values: true, false]

options.name: --tests-only
options.description: Restrict the affected set to **test projects** (those referencing a test framework: Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, xUnit, NUnit, or MSTest). Composes with every `--format`, so `affected --tests-only --format matrix` yields a CI matrix of exactly the tests worth running for this change. Exits `166` when no affected project is a test project

options.name: --exit-zero-on-empty
options.description: Exit 0 instead of 166 when no projects are affected, for pipelines that treat any non-zero exit as failure. Outputs are still written

options.name: --set-variable
options.description: Emit an Azure DevOps `##vso[task.setvariable variable=<NAME>]true|false` logging command to stdout reporting whether **any** project is affected (`true`) or none is (`false`). Lets a pipeline set a job variable natively instead of parsing `--format count` and echoing the logging command by hand, e.g. `- ${{ if eq(variables.affected, 'true') }}:`

options.name: --set-count-variable
options.description: Emit an Azure DevOps `##vso[task.setvariable variable=<NAME>;isOutput=true]<count>` output variable to stdout carrying the affected-project count, consumable across stages (`isOutput=true`). Replaces the hand-rolled count-parse + echo

options.name: --traversal-sdk-version
options.description:
Microsoft.Build.Traversal SDK version pinned in the generated traversal output's `<Project Sdk="...">`
[default: 3.0.3]

options.name: --format
options.description:
Output format. Can be provided more than once or with multiple values
- traversal
- text
- json
- matrix:      GitHub Actions / Azure job-matrix JSON: `{"include":[{"name","path"}]}`, ready to feed a pipeline's `strategy.matrix` so it fans out only over the affected projects
- dotnet-test: One ready-to-run `dotnet test "<path>"` command per affected project — the test-impact run list. Pair with `--tests-only` to emit commands for just the affected test projects
- sarif:       SARIF 2.1.0 impact report: one result per affected project under the `AFFECTED` rule, consumable by GitHub code scanning alongside the `lint`/`format` SARIF so all three surfaces speak one format
- count:       A bare affected-project count written to stdout (no file), e.g. `53` — for CI parallelism math without parsing a file: `affected --tests-only --format count --exit-zero-on-empty`

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Write generated outputs to stdout instead of files

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Print progress and timing information while calculating affected projects

options.name: --output-dir
options.description: Directory where output files are generated. Relative paths are resolved from the repository root

options.name: --output-name
options.description:
Base name for generated output files
[default: affected]

options.name: --exclude-project
options.description: Exclude affected projects whose name or full path matches the regex

options.name: --emit-manifest
options.description: Write a single shared affected manifest (JSON: change range + affected projects + test subset + changed files) to this file. Feed it to `lint`/`build`/`test-plan --projects-file` so the affected set is computed once per CI run and reused instead of recomputed by each command

options.name: --project
options.description: Limit a solution run to specific project paths or project names

options.name: --include
options.description: Relative file or folder paths to include

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Relative file or folder paths to exclude

options.name: --include-generated
options.description: Include generated source files

options.name: --no-restore
options.description: Accepted for dotnet format CLI compatibility. Restore is never performed

options.name: --report
options.description: Directory to receive a JSON report

options.name: --verify-no-changes
options.description: Verify that no formatting changes would be performed

options.name: --diff
options.description: Preview the would-be rewrite as a unified diff (git-apply-able) without writing any file. Shows whitespace, style, and `lint --fix` (CST) edits in one patch. Exits non-zero when any file would change

options.name: --no-cache
options.description: Disable the incremental formatting cache

options.name: --agent
options.description: Optimize output for AI agents: terse, low-token, and ending with the exact follow-up command (e.g. `dotnet-fast lint --fix <target>`) so the agent runs the CLI fixer instead of hand-editing. Forces agent output on. It is also auto-enabled when an AI/agent shell is detected (Claude Code, Cursor, …) or `DOTNET_FAST_AGENT=1` is set

options.name: --human
options.description:
Force rich, human-readable output even when an AI/agent environment is detected (the opt-out for agent auto-detection). Overrides `--agent` is not allowed; the two are mutually exclusive
[alias: --rich]

options.name: --diagnostics
options.description: Limit style and analyzer fixes to the provided diagnostic IDs

options.name: --exclude-diagnostics
options.description: Exclude style and analyzer fixes for the provided diagnostic IDs

options.name: --severity
options.description:
Minimum diagnostic severity to fix
[possible values: hidden, info, warn, error]

options.name: --color
options.description:
When to colorize console output: auto (color a TTY), always, or never. Honors the NO_COLOR and CLICOLOR_FORCE environment conventions
- auto:   Color when stdout is a terminal (the default)
- always: Always color, even when piped or redirected
- never:  Never color
[default: auto]

options.name: --summary
options.description: Collapse fully-fixable whitespace findings in the human `lint` report into a single one-line count, listing only the findings that need a decision. Mirrors what `--agent` already does for AI callers

options.name: --binarylog
options.description: Accepted for CLI compatibility; real MSBuild binary logs are not emitted

options.name: --verbosity
options.description:
Verbosity level: quiet, minimal, normal, detailed, or diagnostic. When no level is supplied, detailed is used
[possible values: quiet, minimal, normal, detailed, diagnostic]

commands.name: build
commands.description: Remote build cache (preview). `build --plan` computes a per-project cache key from its inputs + dependencies and, when a cache URL is configured, probes Azure Blob Storage for a hit/miss — without building. The basis for extracting pre-built artifacts instead of rebuilding on a clean checkout

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --plan
options.description: Compute the cache plan (per-project keys + blob hit/miss) without building, extracting, or uploading. Omit this flag for a cache-backed build that restores hits, builds misses, and uploads trusted misses

options.name: --configuration
options.description: Build configuration the cache key is computed for. Overrides `buildCache.configuration` in `dotnet-fast.json`; defaults to `Release`

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: --projects-file
options.description: Read the exact project set to build from a file. Accepts newline project names/paths, `dotnet test <project>` lines, affected matrix JSON (`include[].path`), or a traversal project (`ProjectReference Include="..."`). Composes with `--ci`/`--from` by intersection

options.name: --read-only
options.description: Read-only cache: restore hits and build misses, but never upload the resulting artifacts. Use on PR/untrusted builds (the main branch populates the cache). Overrides `buildCache.readOnly` in `dotnet-fast.json`

options.name: --fallback
options.description: If the cache is unreachable or not configured, fall back to a plain `dotnet build` instead of failing — so one `dotnet-fast build` invocation covers the cache-hit, cache-miss, and cache-down paths. The fallback builds `--projects-file` (when it is a project/solution/traversal file), else the target, else the current directory

options.name: --assume-restored
options.description: Assert that NuGet restore state already exists for every project — e.g. the pipeline runs a whole-tree `dotnet restore --locked-mode <sln>` before `dotnet-fast build`. Two effects (issue #229): every compile gets `--no-restore`, and projects within a topological layer compile **concurrently** instead of one at a time. Concurrency is tied to this flag on purpose — without it each compile falls through to `dotnet build`'s own implicit restore, and running those at once races on the shared global packages folder (spurious `CS0246`, issue #204). Off by default: with no upfront restore, a project that was not a cache hit has no restore state and `--no-restore` fails it outright (issue #210)

options.name: --build-jobs
options.description:
With `--assume-restored`: maximum projects compiled at once. Defaults to one per logical core. Each `dotnet build` is itself multi-threaded, so a lower number can be faster on a small agent
[default: 0]

options.name: --check
options.description: With `--plan`: turn the plan into a fast availability check for scripting. Exits `0` only when the cache is reachable and *every* project is already cached (a hit) — i.e. safe to skip `dotnet restore`/build and just `dotnet-fast build`. Exits `3` on any miss/un-cacheable project, `4` when the cache is unreachable or not configured

options.description: Scope to affected projects by comparing this revision against --to or the working tree

options.name: --to
options.description: Scope to affected projects by comparing --from against this revision

options.name: --merge-base

options.name: --format
options.description:
Emit a build job-matrix instead of building (#91): the affected build's transitive closure, partitioned into topological **layers** (waves) and sharded within each layer. `matrix` = GitHub Actions (`{"include":[{layer,shard,totalShards}...]}`); `ado-matrix` = Azure DevOps. Pair with `--auto-shards` or `--shards`. The pipeline runs each layer as a sequential wave; agents in a wave build their slice and the next wave restores their outputs. `text` (default) is the normal report
Possible values:
- text:       Human-readable build/plan report (default)
- matrix:     GitHub Actions job-matrix: `{"include":[{layer,shard,totalShards}...]}`
- ado-matrix: Azure DevOps strategy-matrix: `{"L0_s1":{layer,shard,totalShards}...}`
[default: text]

options.name: --shards
options.description: With `--format matrix|ado-matrix`: shards per layer. Pairs with `--shard` as the denominator for a single-shard build

options.name: --auto-shards
options.description: Pick the per-layer shard count from the layer's project count (matrix planning), capped by `--max-shards`. A trivial layer collapses to one shard

options.name: --max-shards
options.description:
Maximum shard count per layer when `--auto-shards` is used
[default: 8]

options.name: --shard
options.description: Build only this layer's shard (1-based). Pairs with `--of` and `--layer`: `build --layer L --shard I --of N` builds layer L's shard I, restoring its dependencies (built by earlier waves) from the cache and uploading its slice

options.name: --of
options.description: Total shards for `--shard` (the denominator). Defaults to `--shards`

options.name: --layer
options.description: Build only this topological layer (0-based wave index), with `--shard`/`--of`

options.name: --timings
options.description: Balance shard assignment by prior-run build duration instead of project count (issue #135). Reads a JSON object mapping a project's file stem to its duration in milliseconds (`{ "MyProject": 1234, … }`); projects absent from the file are estimated from the average of the timed ones. Takes precedence over `--use-cached-timings` when both are given

options.name: --use-cached-timings
options.description: Balance shard assignment by durations stored in the build cache instead of a local `--timings` file — downloads the merged timings blob (written by `--record-timings`) and balances by time, falling back to project count for a project with no recorded duration. Zero pipeline plumbing: no artifact publish/download

options.name: --record-timings
options.description: After a real build, extract this run's per-project build durations and upload them to the build cache (merged with prior runs via a moving average), so future runs can `--use-cached-timings`. Unlike `test-plan --record-timings`, this needs no `--results-dir`: durations come straight from the build itself. Only meaningful on a path that actually builds (bare `build`, or `--layer`/`--shard`); a no-op with `--plan` or `--format matrix`/`ado-matrix`, which never build anything

options.name: --timings-scope
options.description: Scope key for the cached timings blob (`--use-cached-timings` / `--record-timings`). Defaults to `DOTNET_FAST_TIMINGS_SCOPE`, then the current Git branch, then `default`. Key per target branch so a PR balances against trunk's history. Every agent building a shard of the same run should pass the same scope for consistent slicing

options.name: --ci
options.description: Detect the comparison range from the CI environment (GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines, GitLab CI, or Jenkins): pull-request builds diff against the merge base with the target branch; branch (push) builds diff against the previous commit

options.name: --pr-base
options.description: Force pull-request mode: diff against the merge base of this target branch and HEAD (e.g. `--pr-base main`). Overrides --ci detection

options.name: --push
options.description: Force push/branch-build mode: diff against the current commit's parent

options.name: --base
options.description: Diff against the merge base of this ref and HEAD (generic form of --pr-base; e.g. `--base origin/develop`). Overrides --ci detection

options.name: --default-branch
options.description: Override the detected default branch (main/master) used as a fallback base for CI resolution

options.name: --fetch-base
options.description:
Minimal-fetch mode: when the comparison base is missing from a shallow checkout, fetch only the base ref (`git fetch --depth=1 origin <base>`, deepening just enough to find the merge base) instead of unshallowing the whole repository. Lets CI jobs drop `fetch-depth: 0`
[alias: --minimal-fetch]

options.name: --ci-base
options.description:
Push-build baseline used by --ci. `previous-commit` preserves the provider's normal before/parent behavior; `last-successful-build` queries Azure Pipelines' Build API for the last succeeded build on this branch; `last-completed-build` also accepts a `partiallySucceeded` build, for pipelines with a `continueOnError: true` step that would otherwise never advance the baseline (issue #234)
- previous-commit
- last-successful-build
- last-completed-build:  `last-successful-build`, but a `partiallySucceeded` build also counts (issue #234): a pipeline with a `continueOnError: true` step never reaches `succeeded`, so the baseline never advances and the comparison window grows without bound
[default: previous-commit]

options.name: --on-missing-base
options.description:
Fallback when --base remains unresolvable after shallow-clone recovery: fail (default), treat the command as unscoped, or scope to no files
[default: error]
[possible values: error, all, empty]

options.name: --ci-base-fallback
options.description:
Fallback when `--ci-base last-successful-build` itself can't complete (missing SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN/Azure vars, no prior successful build, first build on a new branch). `previous-commit` (default) narrows to HEAD~1 — which silently under-builds a batched trigger; `all` conservatively scopes to every file; `error` fails loudly. Distinct from --on-missing-base, which governs an unresolvable explicit --from/--to/--base
[possible values: previous-commit, all, error]

options.name: --all
options.description:
Accepted as a no-op for range-string compatibility with `affected --all`: `lint`/`build`/`test-plan` already process the whole target by default, so `--all` (with an optional boolean value) simply means "no range scoping" and is silently ignored — even alongside a real scoping flag (`--ci`/`--base`/`--from`), which still governs the range. Lets a pipeline share one resolved range string across `affected` and these commands without stripping `--all` before invoking them
[default: false]
[possible values: true, false]

options.description: Show version information

options.name: --fix-safe-only
options.description: Like `--fix`, but apply only Safe-tier CST (`lint`) autofixes — the redundancy/style cleanups — and hold back behavior-preserving (performance) and suggestion (correctness/concurrency/maintainability) rewrites for review. Whitespace/style/analyzer formatting still applies. `--list-rules`/`--explain` show each rule's tier

options.description: Scope to the files this branch changed: diff against the merge base with the repository's default branch (main/master), including working-tree changes. options.description: Scope to the files currently staged in Git (the index) — the pre-commit hook workflow: lint (or `--fix`) only what you're about to commit. Takes precedence over `--affected`/`--from`/`--ci`

options.name: --watch
options.description: Keep running: after the first pass, watch the target tree and re-run whenever a `.cs`/`.editorconfig`/`.globalconfig` file changes (the warm tree-sitter parser is reused, so re-runs are fast). Exit with Ctrl-C. Cannot be combined with `--diff`, `--staged`, or `--write-baseline`

options.name: --sarif
options.description: Also write a SARIF 2.1.0 report to this path (for CI/PR integration). Text diagnostics are still printed to stdout

options.name: --to
options.description: The Git revision to compare `--from` against. Defaults to the working tree when omitted

options.name: --deep
options.description: Also run the project's real Roslyn analyzers via the .NET sidecar host (StyleCop, Roslynator, Meziantou, Sonar, .NET CA*, etc.) and merge their diagnostics into the report. Requires the .NET SDK + a restored project

options.name: --no-deep
options.description: Force the fast native path even when the `DOTNET_FAST_DEEP` deep-by-default opt-in is set (no effect otherwise). Overrides the env opt-in for this run

options.name: --deep-cache
options.description: Cache `--deep` analyzer diagnostics per project in the build cache, keyed by the project's build key + its editorconfig chain + the host identity. A project whose inputs and rules are unchanged restores its diagnostics instead of re-binding the semantic model, so `--deep` scales with change (#96). Requires a configured build cache; `--read-only` skips uploads (PR runs). Opt-in: keyed strictly larger than the binary cache, but a few non-deterministic analyzers may not be safe to cache

options.name: --baseline
options.description: Suppress findings recorded in this baseline file and report only new ones (exit non-zero only on new findings) — the on-ramp for gating a repo that already has a findings backlog

options.name: --write-baseline
options.description: Write the current findings to the `--baseline` file (snapshot) and exit successfully, instead of comparing against it

options.name: --list-rules
options.description: Print the catalog of native CST lint rules (id, summary, and whether `--fix` can repair it) and exit, without scanning any files

options.name: --explain
options.description: Print the full description and docs link for one native CST rule (e.g. `--explain DF0042`) and exit, without scanning any files

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit `--list-rules` / `--explain` output as JSON (for tooling and docs) instead of the human-readable text

options.name: --category
options.description: With `--list-rules`, show only rules in this category (case-insensitive): Correctness, Concurrency, Performance, Maintainability, Redundancy, Style

options.name: --fixable
options.description: With `--list-rules`, show only autofixable rules (the ones `--fix` rewrites). Combines with `--category`

options.name: --whole-file
options.description: Report lint findings on **every** line of a changed file, not just the lines this branch touched. Opts out of the default changed-line (hunk) scoping that applies to `--staged`, `--ci` (pull-request), `--pr-base`, and `--base`. Use it to surface a file's full backlog when you touch it

options.name: --changed-lines
options.description: Report lint findings only on the lines this branch changed (changed-line / hunk scoping). On by default for `--staged`/`--ci`(PR)/`--pr-base`/`--base`; pass this to force it for explicit `--from`/`--to` and `--ci` push builds

options.name: --fix-changed-lines
options.description: Bound `--fix` (or `--fix-safe-only`) to the same changed-line (hunk) scope this run's report uses (issue #277): no fix pass — whitespace, style, analyzer, or CST — writes a line outside a hunk this invocation would have reported on. With `--exec`: run up to N of the shard's `dotnet test` commands concurrently instead of one at a time (#229 Phase 6). Defaults to `1`, today's strictly sequential behaviour, byte-for-byte. Overlap is only ever startup/IO-wait — REQUIRES `--no-build` in `--test-args`: without it, two containers that share a `ProjectReference` would each run `dotnet test`'s own implicit build, and could compile the same dependency into the same `bin`/`obj` at once (file-in-use/CS2012/torn outputs); the canonical `--restore-from-cache` recipe already restores the tree up front and passes `--no-build`, which satisfies this for free. TRX filenames and `.runsettings` paths are unique per shard+project index and VSTest ports are ephemeral, so concurrent execution itself has no collision to worry about — the implicit-build hazard above is the one precondition a caller must uphold. Combined with `--record-timings`, the entire timings upload (fixture durations *and* startup residuals) is skipped with a notice instead of recorded: durations from a contended run are noise-dominated and would corrupt future shard balancing rather than improve it — keep one `--test-jobs 1` lane if you need fresh recordings
[default: 1]

options.name: --restore-from-cache
options.description: Before running (`--exec`), restore from the build cache exactly this shard's project closure — its test projects plus their transitive dependencies — instead of the caller restoring the whole affected tree in a separate `build --read-only` step. Scopes the per-agent download to the shard's slice (issue #92). Requires `--exec`. With `--fallback`, a missing or unreachable cache builds the shard's closure instead of failing

options.name: --fallback
options.description: With `--restore-from-cache`: if the cache is unconfigured or unreachable, build the shard's closure with the cache-backed builder instead of failing the step (mirrors `build --fallback`)

options.name: --cache-wait
options.description:
With `--restore-from-cache`: seconds to wait for an in-progress cache upload before treating a project as a miss. For pipelines that run the test shards in parallel with the build that populates the cache, waiting briefly is usually far cheaper than every shard rebuilding the closure. `0` (the default) preserves the existing behaviour: a miss falls straight through to a build
[default: 0]

options.name: --cache-wait-share-misses
options.description: With `--cache-wait`: share a give-up across shards (issue #228). A shard matrix runs one process per shard, so a key that is genuinely never coming is re-discovered the hard way by every shard whose closure references it, each burning the whole `--cache-wait` budget. With this flag a shard that exhausts the wait records a small marker blob beside the cache entries, and a later shard — a second wave of a staggered matrix, or a pipeline re-run — skips the wait for that key instead of repeating it. The marker is only consulted *after* a real cache miss and only while it is recent, so a key that has since landed is always restored normally. Needs a cache credential with write access; if the write fails the run continues unshared. Off by default: skipping a wait is only ever right when the key really is absent

options.name: --assume-restored
options.description: With `--restore-from-cache`: assert that NuGet restore state already exists for every project in the shard's closure — e.g. the pipeline runs a whole-tree `dotnet restore --locked-mode` before this step. Mirrors `build --assume-restored` (issue #229): every closure-build compile gets `--no-restore`, and projects within a topological layer compile **concurrently** instead of one at a time. Cache HITS already build with `--no-restore` today (an extracted artifact materializes restore state on its own) — this flag is only about the MISSES in the closure. Off by default: without an upfront restore, a miss has no restore state and `--no-restore` fails it outright with `NETSDK1004` (the #210 class) — only enable this when the shard agent genuinely restored the tree first (or when `--fallback`'s clean-local-build path is expected to cover every project, since that path also never restores)

options.name: --build-jobs
options.description: With `--assume-restored`: maximum shard-closure projects compiled at once. Defaults to one per logical core

options.name: --allow-empty-test-results
options.description:
With `--exec --results-dir`: do NOT fail when a `dotnet test` exits `0` without writing its TRX (issue #238), restoring the pre-v0.306.0 behaviour where such a run counted as a pass.
Since v0.306.0 a missing TRX is an error, because it is *only* ever produced by a run that never started a test host — a shard that reported success having demonstrably tested nothing. A filter that legitimately matches no tests is a different thing and still passes: VSTest writes the TRX either way, with zero counters, so "TRX present, zero tests" is always honest and "TRX absent" is always broken. Only reach for this flag if some project in the shard genuinely cannot produce a TRX (a custom `--logger` in `--test-args` that replaces the trx one, say) and you have another way to prove those tests ran.

options.name: --test-args
options.description: Extra command-line arguments appended to every emitted or executed `dotnet test`, e.g. `--no-build --no-restore -c Release`

options.name: --filter-and
options.description: AND this VSTest filter expression with the generated fixture filter. For whole-project shards it becomes the only `--filter` expression

options.name: --results-dir
options.description: Add TRX logging and write result files under DIR, one file per shard project (`--logger trx;LogFileName=... --results-directory DIR`)

options.description: Add `--collect` to every `dotnet test`. The value `cobertura` expands to `Code Coverage;Format=cobertura`; other values are passed through

options.name: --verify
options.description: Build/run the selected test projects and verify the shard union matches the runtime-discovered test set. Opt-in because it shells out to `dotnet`

options.name: --from
options.description: Scope to affected test projects by comparing this revision against --to or the working tree

options.name: --to
options.description: Scope to affected test projects by comparing --from against this revision

options.name: --merge-base
options.description: Use the merge base of --from and --to when scoping affected test projects

options.name: --exit-zero-on-empty
options.description: Exit 0 instead of 166 when scoping (`--from`/`--ci`/`--cache-misses-file`) leaves no test project to shard, for pipelines that treat any non-zero exit as failure. The (empty) plan is still emitted

options.name: --fail-on-skipped-projects
options.description: Exit `167` when a project classified as a test project contributes no fixtures (or only part of its fixtures) to the plan — its source language is not parsed, its sources are missing or unparsable, or it declares no test fixture at all. Such projects are ALWAYS warned about on stderr and listed in `--format json` / `--report` as `skippedProjects`; this flag turns that warning into a hard failure. Off by default because a scaffolded-but-still-empty test project is legitimate — turn it on once your repo has none, and a test project that silently stops contributing tests can never report green again

options.name: --ci
options.description: Detect the comparison range from the CI environment (GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines, GitLab CI, or Jenkins): pull-request builds diff against the merge base with the target branch; branch (push) builds diff against the previous commit

options.name: --pr-base
options.description: Force pull-request mode: diff against the merge base of this target branch and HEAD (e.g. `--pr-base main`). Overrides --ci detection

options.name: --push
options.description: Force push/branch-build mode: diff against the current commit's parent

options.name: --base
options.description: Diff against the merge base of this ref and HEAD (generic form of --pr-base; e.g. `--base origin/develop`). Overrides --ci detection

options.name: --default-branch
options.description: Override the detected default branch (main/master) used as a fallback base for CI resolution

options.name: --fetch-base
options.description:
Minimal-fetch mode: when the comparison base is missing from a shallow checkout, fetch only the base ref (`git fetch --depth=1 origin <base>`, deepening just enough to find the merge base) instead of unshallowing the whole repository. Lets CI jobs drop `fetch-depth: 0`
[alias: --minimal-fetch]

options.name: --ci-base
options.description:
Push-build baseline used by --ci. `previous-commit` preserves the provider's normal before/parent behavior; `last-successful-build` queries Azure Pipelines' Build API for the last succeeded build on this branch; `last-completed-build` also accepts a `partiallySucceeded` build, for pipelines with a `continueOnError: true` step that would otherwise never advance the baseline (issue #234)
- previous-commit
- last-successful-build
- last-completed-build:  `last-successful-build`, but a `partiallySucceeded` build also counts (issue #234): a pipeline with a `continueOnError: true` step never reaches `succeeded`, so the baseline never advances and the comparison window grows without bound
[default: previous-commit]

options.name: --on-missing-base
options.description:
Fallback when --base remains unresolvable after shallow-clone recovery: fail (default), treat the command as unscoped, or scope to no files
[default: error]
[possible values: error, all, empty]

options.name: --ci-base-fallback
options.description:
Fallback when `--ci-base last-successful-build` itself can't complete (missing SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN/Azure vars, no prior successful build, first build on a new branch). `previous-commit` (default) narrows to HEAD~1 — which silently under-builds a batched trigger; `all` conservatively scopes to every file; `error` fails loudly. Distinct from --on-missing-base, which governs an unresolvable explicit --from/--to/--base
[possible values: previous-commit, all, error]

options.name: --all
options.description:
Accepted as a no-op for range-string compatibility with `affected --all`: `lint`/`build`/`test-plan` already process the whole target by default, so `--all` (with an optional boolean value) simply means "no range scoping" and is silently ignored — even alongside a real scoping flag (`--ci`/`--base`/`--from`), which still governs the range. Lets a pipeline share one resolved range string across `affected` and these commands without stripping `--all` before invoking them
[default: false]
[possible values: true, false]
